blockMcqs.question: One business transaction must span several services. What fits?
options: A saga with compensating actions
A single ACID transaction
A read replica
A pub/sub notification
blockMcqs.explanation: Cross-service atomicity is impossible, so local steps undo via compensation.

blockMcqs.question: Which statement about events versus commands is correct?
options: An event can be rejected by its handler
A command is a past-tense immutable fact
A command can be rejected; an event cannot
One event always produces exactly one command
blockMcqs.explanation: A command asks and may be refused; an event already happened.

blockMcqs.question: Why does event sourcing need a streaming log, not plain pub/sub?
options: Pub/sub guarantees stricter ordering
A log lets new consumers replay history from offset 0
Pub/sub stores events forever by default
Logs avoid the need for idempotency
blockMcqs.explanation: Pub/sub forgets after delivery, so past events and rebuilds are lost.

blockMcqs.question: What role does a snapshot play in event sourcing?
options: It is the authoritative source of truth
It replaces the event log entirely
It records command rejections
It speeds replay and can always be rebuilt
blockMcqs.explanation: Snapshots are a cache; the log remains the only source of truth.

blockMcqs.question: In CQRS, what must the read (query) side never do?
options: Run business logic or write data
Serve denormalized views
Consume the event stream
Be rebuilt by replaying from offset 0
blockMcqs.explanation: All decisions live on the command side; leaked writes break CQRS.

blockMcqs.question: A saga step fails after earlier steps committed. What happens?
options: A global rollback reverts every step
Compensating actions semantically undo prior steps
Two-phase commit locks all services
The whole saga is silently discarded
blockMcqs.explanation: Committed steps can't be reversed, so you append counteracting actions.

blockMcqs.question: How does the transactional outbox avoid the dual-write problem?
options: It publishes to the broker before the DB write
It uses two-phase commit across DB and broker
It writes the event into the same DB transaction
It retries the broker publish until it succeeds
blockMcqs.explanation: One atomic commit means the event can't be lost or fabricated.

blockMcqs.question: What is the single most important signal to watch in EDA?
options: CPU usage on the broker
Number of event types defined
Consumer / projection lag
Total disk used by the log
blockMcqs.explanation: Rising lag means read models are stale and falling further behind.

blockMcqs.question: Why is relying on a broker's exactly-once flag risky?
options: Exactly-once delivery is unattainable; build idempotent consumers
It forces synchronous calls everywhere
It disables the transactional outbox
It makes events mutable on retry
blockMcqs.explanation: You get at-least-once delivery; idempotency yields exactly-once effects.
